about: The archivist's catalogue: every kind of error found so far, why it happened, what fixed it and what guards it. Edited by a person; the archivist reads it on every run (archivist.py). No requirement text from Karimi's postings except the short examples a person chose.

entries.title: A degree the rules did not read as one
entries.cause: Degree names and the words in front of them the rules did not know (BS, BA/BS, B.E., HBO, WO, 'Relevant bachelor's or master's'), so the atom was read as a skill.
entries.example: BA/BS Degree in STEM -> 'BA/BS Degree in STEM' instead of Bachelor in STEM

entries.title: A degree's field that is not a field
entries.cause: An alternative after the degree glued into its field: 'or relevant experience', a second degree, a language.
entries.example: Bachelor's degree or relevant experience -> 'Bachelor in or relevant experience'

entries.title: 'is a plus' or 'preferred' left at the end of a requirement
entries.cause: Only words in front were taken as how much it is wanted; a closing 'is a plus' stayed in the requirement and made a new one.
entries.example: Experience with Go is a plus -> 'Go is a plus' instead of Go, optional

residual.measured_on: batch 1 of the new postings, rules 0.4.2, library re-run 2026-11-16

entries.title: A requirement read as 'Desirable' alone
entries.cause: An atom opening on how much it is wanted ('Desirable', 'Advantageous', 'Preferred', 'Optional') is read as if that word were the requirement: the object after it is lost and the atom still counts.
entries.example: Desirable experience in design -> 'Desirable', counted

entries.title: A requirement left in another language
entries.cause: The translator knew seven languages; Chinese, Japanese, Polish, Lithuanian, Hungarian and others were kept as written and nearly all came out 'nuovo'.
entries.example: Laisvas anglų kalbos mokėjimas -> kept as written

entries.title: Translated, and still not English
entries.cause: A language sent to the wrong model (Polish through the Romance one, until 0.4.2), or a model that cannot read it.
entries.example: Wykształcenie wyższe w zakresie takim jak Informatyka -> unchanged after 'translation'

entries.title: The curator joined a category to a broader one
entries.cause: Taking a vendor or a generic word off in front of a category ('SAP EAM' -> 'EAM', 'IT platforms' -> 'IT'), and the judge passed it.
entries.example: IT platforms -> IT

entries.title: The batch chose the language differently from the API
entries.cause: translate_must_have.py kept its own copy of which language and which model, so the dictionary missed what the library had learnt (0.9% of items).
entries.example: Polish items translated with the Romance model in the dictionary only

entries.title: A rule silently dead: a backspace where \b was meant
entries.cause: Patches written through a shell heredoc turned \b into a backspace character in two 0.4.1 patterns.
entries.example: Master's student never read as a student

entries.title: 'as a plus', 'an added advantage' left in the requirement
entries.cause: The rules take off the closing words that say how much it is wanted only from a fixed list; 'as a plus', 'is an added advantage', 'also welcome', 'of advantage' are not on it.
entries.example: Financial services industry knowledge as a plus -> key keeps 'as a plus'

entries.title: 'required' or 'a must' left in the requirement
entries.cause: A closing 'required', 'mandatory', 'is a must' says how it is asked, like 'is a plus', and no rule takes it off.
entries.example: CISSP or CISM certification required -> key keeps 'required'

entries.title: 'or similar role' left in the requirement
entries.cause: 'or similar', 'or equivalent', 'or related' add nothing (the counting guide) and are taken off after degrees only.
entries.example: 3+ years as a Data Engineer or similar role -> key 'Data Engineer or similar role'

entries.title: A level ('Advanced', 'Intermediate') left in the requirement
entries.cause: Skill grids put the level after the name ('<skill> Advanced'); the level rules read it only in front.
entries.example: LangChain Intermediate -> key 'LangChain Intermediate'

entries.title: 'Higher education' not read as a degree
entries.cause: 'Higher education' / 'University education' with fields in a bracket is not among the degree names.
entries.example: Higher Education (Electric Engineering, Automation Engineering) -> key 'Higher Education'

entries.title: A split that leaves a piece with no sense
entries.cause: A head distributed to the wrong part, or a cut inside a phrase: the piece no longer names anything.
entries.example: Ability to proactively learn new concepts and technology -> 'Ability to technology'
entries.fix_hint: No reliable detector: the shape rules were right on at most 22% (2026-11-07). Watched by the explorer.

entries.title: A list left in one requirement
entries.cause: A list before 'and services like ...' or with a category in it is kept whole.
entries.example: Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and services like Kafka -> 'Docker, Kubernetes, and services'
entries.fix_hint: No reliable detector (list_not_separated in split_flags was imprecise). Watched by the explorer.

entries.title: An acronym ending in S read as a plural
entries.cause: The fold that joins a plural to its singular (normalise_req.canon) takes the S off an acronym, so IDMS and IDM, HRIS and HRI become one key.
entries.example: SAP IDM joined by the curator to IDMS

entries.title: Activities sharing one object split apart
entries.cause: Nouns or gerunds of activity before one object (design, deployment and support of X) were split, leaving the first ones with no object.
entries.example: Experience in design, deployment and support of network solutions -> design, deployment, support of network solutions

entries.title: A frame word left in the requirement
entries.cause: Frames the rules did not know: knowledge about X, several frame nouns at once (qualifications/experience/knowledge of X), a German frame glued on (X-Kenntnisse), years written out (five years of progressively responsible experience). The user's review of batch 3 (2026-11-18) found more: `Interest in`, `programming with`, `using ... as`, `popular`/`modern`/`scalable`, `concepts of`, `Registered studies in`. Since 0.4.5 the inspector detects the shape (`frame_left`).
entries.example: Practical knowledge about microservices -> about microservices

entries.title: A language requirement not read as a language
entries.cause: A translated language requirement with words the language rule did not accept (I hear English is very fluent, from the Chinese for listen, speak, read, write).
entries.example: I hear English is very fluent in reading and writing -> kept whole

entries.title: A language read as another, or not at all
entries.cause: The word lists took Danish for Swedish and did not know Finnish or some Czech, so they went to the wrong model or none.
entries.example: Erfaring med at afdække behov -> Experience with afdække needs

entries.title: A named technology kept inside the words around it
entries.cause: The core kept the activity or the category beside the name, so the same technology landed in many groups. The user's call of 2026-11-17: the name wins, the rest goes to extra.
entries.example: Cloud engineering experience on Azure -> Cloud engineering experience on Azure

entries.title: Named examples read as words of their category
entries.cause: `such as`, `e.g.` and brackets of names were glued to the category or dropped. The user's call of 2026-11-17: named examples are the requirements, the category goes; common-noun examples and what `including` adds stay with the category.
entries.example: ERP systems such as SAP or Oracle -> ERP systems SAP

entries.title: An atom starting with a comma
entries.cause: A list cut on the wrong side of its comma.
entries.example: , and cybersecurity frameworks

entries.title: A list left in one requirement
entries.cause: Adjective lists, `with the ability to` and `eager to learn` were not split.
entries.example: Curious, open-minded, eager to learn -> one requirement

entries.title: A preposition left at the edge of a requirement
entries.cause: The frame was cut one word too late or too early.
entries.example: working on CPaaS -> on CPaaS

entries.title: The same requirement twice in one item
entries.cause: A head distributed over a list whose items normalise to one key.
entries.example: Systems thinking x3 in one item

entries.title: A language read as its level or as a skill
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): The frame parse took the level or a word around the language for the object.
entries.example: Minimum English level C1 -> C1

entries.title: Where or what for left in the requirement
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): `in a fast paced environment`, `within a mission-critical environment`, `to interact with stakeholders` stayed in the key; they are context for `extra`.
entries.example: leading technical projects in a fast paced environment

entries.title: A name kept with a word that adds nothing
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): `Domain`, `Methodologies`, `software development` after a name kept it from winning.
entries.example: Dominio avanzado de SQL -> SQL Domain

entries.title: A verb alone, its object lost
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): A run of verbs over one object cut after the first verb.
entries.example: take on, understand and maintain legacy codebases -> take

entries.title: Named examples set aside while the requirement names nothing
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): A bracket of names after a gerund or a vague holder (`affinity`) went to extra.
entries.example: orchestrating hybrid-cloud infrastructures (AWS, Azure, VMware) -> orchestrating hybrid-cloud infrastructures

entries.title: A word cut from the noun it shared
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): `national and EU financing mechanisms` split as `national` and `EU financing mechanisms`.
entries.example: national

entries.title: The item's first requirement glued in front of the others
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): `including` over a list that is not all names distributed the head.
entries.example: AI literacy, including prompt engineering -> AI literacy prompt engineering

entries.title: Activities left in front of the object
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4 (37 of 100 wrong, the inspector had flagged 2): Coordinated gerunds before one object are one ask and the object is what is asked (2026-10-29).
entries.example: training and evaluating machine learning models

entries.title: Roles in alternative left in one requirement
entries.cause: The user's review of batch 4: 'working as an Azure Cloud Architect, Lead Architect or Design Architect' was one key with three roles. The user's call (2026-11-18): the same role written several ways is one requirement, that role; different roles are separate requirements.
entries.example: Experience as a Data Engineer or Data Scientist

entries.title: The requirement left empty, what is asked set aside
entries.cause: A word in front of the frame noun the rules did not know as a level (high, perfect, confirmed, foundational, expert-level) or as a kind of experience (implementation, production) became the core; the junk filter then emptied it, and the object stayed in extra.
entries.example: High proficiency in Python -> '' (Python in extra) instead of Python, level strong

entries.title: Names before a category dropped
entries.cause: When every example after 'such as / like' was a name, the lead before the category was discarded, with the names it listed.
entries.example: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and frameworks like Angular or React -> Angular, React only

entries.title: Several clauses, each with its own frame, left in one
entries.cause: A line of several asks ('3+ years of experience in A, B, strong knowledge of C, and experience with D (E, F)') was split as one list: the last bracket was read as the list for everything and the line came back whole (route llm). 55 of the 109 comma_in_key flags of batch 5.
entries.example: 3+ years of experience in Python, SQL and Spark, strong knowledge of Docker ... -> one requirement

entries.title: A 'Header: a, b, c' header glued onto its items
entries.cause: After a colon under a header that is no name, with a mix of names and common nouns, the header was put in front of every item and kept as an atom of its own.
entries.example: Strong backend fundamentals: PostgreSQL, async workflows, queues -> 'backend fundamentals queues'

entries.title: School diplomas and student status not read as education
entries.cause: No level for the school-leaving diploma; 'Currently enrolled in a', 'Hold a', 'Be a graduate of a' were not words the rules accept in front of a degree; 'Masters’', 'STEM degree', 'Bac +5 en', 'Hbo', a degree after years of experience.
entries.example: Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in business -> not education

entries.title: A level or kind word read as what is asked
entries.cause: A word in front of the frame the rules did not know as a level ('recent'): it became the core, the object went to extra.
entries.example: Recent hands-on experience with Braze is preferable -> 'Recent' instead of Braze

entries.title: Years the rules did not read
entries.cause: Years written after the number in a way the rules did not know ('1 year minimum').
entries.example: 1 year minimum with Boomi -> 'minimum with Boomi' instead of Boomi, 1 year

entries.title: A willingness to travel reduced to the place
entries.cause: The rule that a name wins over the words around it took the country out of 'Willingness to travel to the United States'.
entries.example: Willingness to travel to the United States -> 'United States'

entries.title: A role cut to its job word
entries.cause: Seniority words in alternative ('Senior, Staff or Lead') were read as roles, and the shared role was cut to its last word.
entries.example: Extensive experience as a Senior, Staff or Lead Software Engineer -> 'Engineer'

entries.title: 'Written and verbal' left in the requirement
entries.cause: How it is communicated was part of the key, so each pair of modes made its own requirement.
entries.example: Clear written and verbal communication skills -> 'written and verbal communication skills'

entries.title: An attitude in front of an object that stands alone
entries.cause: 'keen eye for', 'passionate about' kept in front of what is asked; by the user's call of 2026-11-23 they go when what follows stands alone and is not one generic word.
entries.example: Curiosity and a keen eye for spotting patterns in data -> 'keen eye for spotting patterns'

entries.title: Coordinated verbs read as one requirement, or the verb dropped
entries.cause: Until 2026-11-23 the rule was 'building and maintaining X' = one requirement, the verbs dropped; the user reversed it: with a generic object each verb is a requirement and keeps its object.
entries.example: designing and implementing complex solutions -> 'complex solutions' instead of two
